title: Mako: Speculative Distributed Transactions with Geo-Replication
problem: Distributed transactions across geographically replicated systems face high latency from synchronous coordination needed to maintain consistency. Traditional approaches require waiting for acknowledgment from multiple geo-distributed replicas before transaction commitment.
motivation: Efficiently executing distributed transactions with strong consistency guarantees across globally distributed data centers is critical for modern cloud databases.
method: The system uses speculative execution where transactions tentatively execute at replica sites before full quorum acknowledgment, reducing round-trip latency. Consistency is maintained through validation and abort protocols that handle incorrect speculation. Different strategies apply to read-only versus update transactions, with coordination mechanisms ensuring correctness.
key_novelty: Speculative execution of distributed transactions in geo-replicated systems that reduces latency while maintaining strong consistency guarantees.
contributions: Speculative execution framework for geo-replicated distributed transactions
Consistency protocols for speculative validation and abort handling
Latency reduction for globally distributed transaction workloads
limitations: Limitations regarding failure mode handling and specific consistency model tradeoffs not discussed with title-only analysis.
